engineering_decisions: Installed pnpm 9.0.6 globally via npm because pnpm was not on PATH and corepack was unavailable. The handoff explicitly mandates pnpm + lockfile, so this preserves the frozen toolchain rather than swapping to npm.

Pinned dependency versions explicitly in package.json (no caret-only ranges) so the generated pnpm-lock.yaml reflects deterministic versions consistent with @crxjs/vite-plugin 2.0.0-beta.25 + vite 5.2.10 + typescript 5.4.5 + vitest 1.5.0.

Used @crxjs/vite-plugin's defineManifest helper in vite.config.ts to satisfy strict TS typing of the imported manifest.json. This is a low-impact engineering wiring choice — the manifest's product semantics are unchanged.
Added /// <reference lib=webworker /> + declare const self: ServiceWorkerGlobalScope in src/background/sw.ts so MV3 SW types resolve under strict TS. WebWorker added to tsconfig.lib.
Added defensive iframe guard (window.top === window.self) in src/content/index.ts. Manifest already sets all_frames=false, so this is belt-and-suspenders for unit-1's empty stub.
Added eslint no-restricted-globals for fetch / XMLHttpRequest / WebSocket as a coarse FPD-4 guard. The proper RU-12 hostname-aware custom rule lands in a later unit per file_plan.
Removed manifest.json from tsconfig.include because @crxjs/vite-plugin already imports it via assert{type:json}; including it in tsc twice produced duplicate-typing noise.

deviations_from_handoff.detail: Installed pnpm via `npm install -g pnpm@9.0.6` because pnpm was not on PATH. This is consistent with the frozen toolchain (pnpm), not a substitution. No semantic deviation.

manifest.json declares an empty `icons` object. The handoff did not specify icon assets for unit-1, and inventing icon files would be a product/UX decision outside allowed_decisions. Default Chrome puzzle-piece icon is shown in chrome://extensions until icons are provided in a later unit.
